task: Section 20 required fixed-point catalog. Full underlying data in seed_relation_iso.json (per-N summary) and seed_fixed_point_full_catalog.json (full classified list of every fixed-point representative, N=1..4).

enumeration_boundary.reason: Total relations on N elements = 2^(N^2). N=4 gives 65536 -- fully exhaustive with isomorphism reduction via all 4!=24 relabelings, completed in ~15s. N=5 gives 2^25=33,554,432 raw relations; exhaustive isomorphism classification would require ~33.5M x 5!=120 = ~4 billion permutation-applications, judged infeasible within this run's practical compute. No sampling is substituted -- per the governing instruction, sampling is never labeled exhaustive, and no principled probability measure on 'the' relations of interest was available to justify a non-exhaustive claim of completeness. N=5+ is left OPEN for enumeration, not estimated.

catalog.canonical_candidates: None uniquely selected -- 2462 nonisomorphic fixed points at this size alone.
catalog.stability_class: Full 1-edge-flip perturbation study performed on all 2462 representatives (see seed_stability.json): average 91.96% of single-edge perturbations remain fixed; 1126 of 2462 (45.8%) are locally maximally stable (survive EVERY single-edge flip); 0 are maximally unstable (every fixed point survives at least one perturbation).

growth_pattern: Fixed-point iso-class count grows 0 (trivial only) -> 6 -> 70 -> 2462 for N=1,2,3,4 -- strictly increasing and not converging to a bounded or unique value across the tested range. This growth pattern is itself evidence against eventual uniqueness (Outcome G), though N<=4 cannot prove non-convergence for all N.
gamma_operator_note: Two versions of the color-refinement quotient operator were tested: Gamma_1 (single pass) and Gamma_infty (iterate quotient-then-refine to convergence). Gamma_1 was found NOT to be idempotent in general (4 of 104 iso-classes at N=3, 59 of 3044 at N=4 exhibit further collapse when their one-shot quotient is independently re-refined from a blank coloring -- because the quotient graph can itself carry a nontrivial automorphism that a fresh 1-WL run cannot break). Gamma_infty is provably and numerically-verified idempotent (0 failures at every tested N). Critically, the FIXED-POINT SET itself is IDENTICAL for both operators (verified: Gamma_infty's 'no collapse at all' class count equals Gamma_1's fixed count exactly at every N: 2=2, 6=6, 70=70, 2462=2462) -- because no collapse operator can ever increase vertex count, so a relation with zero first-round collapse is automatically a true fixed point of either operator. The distinction only matters for the INTERMEDIATE trajectory of relations that do collapse, not for the seed-closure question itself.
